title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview
This document defines Redwood Inference’s standardized policies and operating procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, procurement and purchase approval, contract intake and lifecycle management, and revenue recognition and billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and functional budget owners across the company.

Purpose and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single reference that drives consistent financial planning, good procurement hygiene, legal review guardrails, and compliant revenue recognition.
- Scope: Applies to all legal entities and business units of Redwood Inference. Covers: annual/quarterly budgeting, monthly rolling forecasts, purchase requisitions and purchase orders (POs), contract review and signature authority, standard contract templates, billing, invoicing and revenue recognition (ASC 606 principles).

Key definitions
- Budget Owner: Named individual accountable for preparing and owning line-item budgets and forecasts for a cost center.
- Forecast: Rolling 12-month estimate updated monthly.
- PO (Purchase Order): Finance-approved purchase instrument used to commit spend to a vendor.
- RevRec: Revenue recognition under ASC 606 (identify contract, performance obligations, transaction price, allocate, recognize).

Governance and roles
- Head of Finance: policy owner and final approver for budget governance exceptions.
- Finance Business Partner: supports budget owners, performs variance analysis, and consolidates forecasts.
- Procurement Coordinator: manages preferred-vendor lists, POs, and vendor onboarding.
- Legal Counsel: reviews non-standard contracts, vendor terms with material data, security, or IP implications.
- Budget Owners: functional managers (product, engineering, sales, ops) who produce budgets and maintain stewardship of spend against budget.

Budgeting and forecasting process
1) Annual budgeting cycle (timeline)
   - Kickoff: September — Finance issues budget templates and assumptions (revenue targets, hiring plan, headcount model).
   - Draft submission: October — Teams submit draft budgets using the standard template (capex/opex, headcount by role band).
   - Review & reconciliation: November — Finance performs cross-functional reviews, headcount validation, and compensation modeling.
   - Final approval: December — Executive team approves the budget; budget is loaded into ERP for the new fiscal year.
2) Rolling forecast
   - Monthly rolling 12-month forecast updated by Budget Owners and consolidated by Finance Business Partners.
   - Forecast changes >5% of line or >$250k require commentary and business rationale.
3) Assumptions and scenario planning
   - All budgets must include stated assumptions for growth, pricing, customer churn, and hiring ramp.
   - Sensitivity scenarios: base, upside (+10–20% revenue), and downside (-10–20% revenue).
4) Reporting and controls
   - Monthly variance reports (actual vs. forecast) delivered to each budget owner within 10 business days of month close.
   - Budgetary controls: spend against budget cannot exceed 100% without an approved reforecast and sign-off.

Budget templates and required fields
- Required fields: cost center, GL account, budget owner, description, FY total, quarterly phasing, headcount FTEs, justification.
- Capital vs Operating: CapEx requests must include business case, expected useful life, and depreciation schedule.

Procurement and purchase approval workflow
1) Purchase requisition (PR)
   - Initiated by budget owner or delegated purchaser in procurement system. PR must reference budget line and include vendor, scope, estimate, and required delivery date.
2) Approval thresholds (finance + procurement + legal involvement)
   - <= $5,000: Manager approval (no PO required for recurring SaaS if covered by contract).
   - $5,001–$25,000: Director approval + Procurement creates PO.
   - $25,001–$100,000: VP approval + Procurement + Finance validation.
   - $100,001–$1,000,000: CFO approval + Procurement + Legal review (if material).
   - > $1,000,000: CEO + CFO + Legal review and Board notification for capital commitments.
3) Preferred vendors and competitive sourcing
   - Procurement maintains a preferred vendor list. Competitive sourcing (2–3 bids) is required for purchases > $50k unless exempted. Exemptions require documented rationale.
4) PO issuance and receiving
   - Procurement issues PO. Goods/services must be receipted in system. Invoices matched against PO and receipt (3-way match) before payment.
5) Emergency procurements
   - Emergency purchases follow an expedited approval path but must be retroactively logged and justified within 3 business days.

Contracts and legal process
1) Contract intake and triage
   - All contracts must be submitted to Legal via the intake form. Pre-approved standard templates are available in the Contract Template Library.
   - Triage criteria: data sensitivity, revenue/commitment size, indemnities, IP, security requirements, and third-party subprocessors.
2) Standard templates and playbooks
   - Standard SaaS Agreement (subscription + usage), Master Services Agreement (MSA), Statement of Work (SOW), NDA, and Reseller Agreement templates exist and should be used without deviation where possible.
3) Legal review thresholds
   - Standard templates and NDAs < $100k: Legal operational review (turnaround 2 business days).
   - Non-standard or material contract terms, revenue commitments >= $100k, or contracts with sensitive data/processors: Legal full review and security review (SLA: 5–10 business days depending on complexity).
4) Signature authority
   - Managers: no external signature authority.
   - Directors: may sign standard NDAs and low-risk vendor forms up to $25k (with legal pre-approval).
   - VP: may sign contracts up to $250k (pre-approved templates only).
   - CFO: may sign contracts up to $1,000,000.
   - CEO: signs contracts > $1,000,000 or where there is material strategic impact.
   - All signatories must confirm budget availability and attach the approved PO (if applicable).
5) Contract change management
   - Material amendments and change orders require re-evaluation of revenue recognition, obligations, and risk; Legal and Finance must sign off.

Revenue recognition and billing policies (high level)
- Accounting framework: Redwood follows ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent) principles for revenue recognition. Key steps below are applied consistently for subscriptions, usage-based services, and professional services.
1) Identify the contract
   - A valid contract exists when there is approval from both parties, enforceable rights/obligations, and commercial substance.
2) Identify performance obligations
   - Typical obligations: platform access (subscription), usage-delivered tokens/embeddings (usage metering), professional services (SOW deliverables).
3) Determine transaction price
   - Consider variable consideration (usage, discounts, credits, refunds). Apply the expected-value or most-likely amount method depending on contract characteristics.
4) Allocate transaction price to performance obligations
   - Use stand-alone selling prices where available. Document assumptions for allocation.
5) Recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied
   - Subscriptions: recognized ratably over the subscription term (over time).
   - Usage-based billing: recognized as services are delivered (measured by usage metered in platform logs).
   - Professional services: recognized based on milestone completion or percentage-of-completion when reliable measures exist.
6) Billing and invoicing practices
   - Default billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly/quarterly in advance for subscription depending on contract terms. Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated.
   - Invoices generated from billing system must include contract reference, invoice period, and customer PO (when provided).
7) Deferred revenue and contract liabilities
   - Cash collected in advance recorded as deferred revenue (contract liability) and amortized into revenue over the service period.
8) Contract modifications and renewals
   - Changes are assessed under ASC 606: determine whether to treat as separate contract, modification, or termination; document judgments and impact on revenue recognition.
9) Credit, refunds, disputes, and bad debt
   - Credits must be approved by Finance. Refunds are rare and require VP/Finance approval. Collections escalate past 60 days: Account Manager -> Collections -> Legal. Reserve policy for bad debt reviewed quarterly.

Controls, auditability, and documentation
- Required artefacts for each contract/purchase: signed contract, approved PO (if required), invoice, receipt/acceptance evidence, GL coding, and budget sign-off.
- Segregation of duties: requisitioners cannot approve their own invoices.
- Internal audit: Finance provides quarterly samples for audit and compliance testing.
- Retention: financial records (contracts, invoices) retained per retention schedule: 7 years for tax-relevant documents unless legal hold applies.

Operational checklists (quick reference)
- New vendor onboarding: Vendor form -> security questionnaire -> procurement approval -> PO -> contract (if required) -> payment terms set in ERP.
- Contract review flow: Intake -> Legal triage -> Security review (if required) -> Commercial/Finance sign-off -> Signatory executes -> Contract uploaded to CLM and linked to PO/invoice.

Escalations and exceptions
- Exceptions to procurement thresholds or contract templates require documented business justification and sign-off from Head of Finance and Legal.
- Urgent escalations (legal, security, or regulatory blocking): notify Head of Legal and Head of Security immediately and log the incident in the contract intake tracker.
